section_summary: This section concludes an American Embassy digest of June 1944 Japanese-language press in Argentina, covering community notices, wartime propaganda, the reopening of Japanese schools, association affairs, and the finances of a Buenos Aires horticultural cooperative. It is followed by diplomatic reporting from Moscow and Stockholm on Japanese political resolve, industrial rationalization, and government-regulated barter. A final Chungking telegram summarizes Chinese newspaper commentary on the war, air power, the occupation and postwar control of Japan, the Allied landings in southern France, and official corruption.

subfiles.title: Digest of Japanese-language newspapers in Argentina for June 1944
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: A digest of Japanese-language newspaper reporting on Argentina’s Japanese community, wartime propaganda, schools, associations, and commercial affairs during June 1944.
subfiles.summary: The continuing digest records Seizo Ikeda’s death and funeral, personal and commercial notices, community events, and the reopening of Japanese-language schools in Buenos Aires Province. Editorial summaries repeat Japanese claims of victories in China and the Marianas, defend the Pearl Harbor attack, and assert the loyalty of Japanese residents of Argentina. Association reports cover recreational events, charitable contributions, the Japanese Association’s administrative decisions, and warnings about fraudulent mail notices in Misiones. The document closes with a detailed balance sheet and profit-and-loss account for the Buenos Aires Horticulturalists’ Association.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on press coverage of Koiso’s governors’ conference remarks
subfiles.about: Reports the unusually prominent Soviet press treatment of Prime Minister Koiso’s call for the Japanese people to prepare for extraordinary circumstances.
subfiles.summary: Moscow: Koiso's remarks to Japan's prefectural governors got a six-inch report in the August 29 Soviet press, more space than Soviet papers usually give Japanese domestic news.

subfiles.title: Japanese Economics: Rationalization of Labor and Materials
subfiles.about: Summarizes German-language newspaper reports on Japanese model factories and a government-controlled barter system.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: Japan's Armaments Ministry introduced German-style "model establishments" scored on a 100-point index, and the Trade Ministry organized barter through a public company with branches in every town, fixed valuations and points, to mobilize goods left idle by closed small and medium businesses.

subfiles.title: Weekly Press Summary, Chungking telegram no. 1444
subfiles.from: Clarence E. Gauss, Chungking, via Navy
subfiles.about: Summarizes Chinese newspaper editorials on the Shanghai war anniversary, Chinese air power, postwar control of Japan, the Allied invasion of southern France, and corruption.
subfiles.summary: Chinese newspapers marked the Shanghai anniversary by urging mobilization, collaboration with American forces, and a Chinese counteroffensive to recover occupied territory. Air Force Day editorials credited American and Russian assistance while calling for a strong indigenous aircraft industry. Several papers advocated Japan’s unconditional surrender, disarmament, occupation, democratization, and prolonged international supervision, with some supporting a permanent American defense belt across the Pacific. Other commentary welcomed the Allied landings in southern France and called for administrative reform, adequate official salaries, and punishment of corruption in China.
